memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the people saw that Moses was so long in coming down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, 'Come, make us gods who will go before us. As for this fellow Moses who brought us up out of Egypt, we don't know what has happened to him.'" - Exod 32:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice what triggered Israel's great sin. Not persecution. Not hunger. Just a delay. Moses had been on the mountain forty days, and the waiting became unbearable. In that gap between promise and fulfilment, the people's hearts drifted.

Waiting is one of the hardest spiritual disciplines. When God seems slow, our minds start filling the silence with our own solutions. Israel did not become atheists — they wanted gods who would "go before us." They wanted guidance they could see, control and carry. That is usually how idolatry begins with us too. Not by rejecting God outright, but by growing impatient with His timing and reaching for something more immediate.

See also how quickly they dismissed Moses — "this fellow Moses." The man God had used to part the sea became "this fellow." Ungrateful hearts have short memories.

Christ knows the ache of waiting. He waited thirty silent years before His ministry began, and He waits even now at the Father's right hand until the appointed day (Heb 10:12-13). If you are in a season of delay, do not mistake God's silence for God's absence. He is not late.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you been waiting on God for, and how is that waiting shaping your heart?
2. When God seems slow, what do you reach for instead of Him?
3. Is there a past mercy of God you have started to speak of lightly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me to wait without wandering. When I cannot see what You are doing, help me to trust who You are. Amen.
